issue_context.title: xmltojson conversion in rest sensor only supports Content-Type text/xml
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->
In version 0.106.0 xmltojson conversion was introduced in the rest sensor. I figured out, that currently there is only the Content-Type text/xml supported. In my installation i would like to use the rest sensor for a resource with Content-Type application/xml, but the conversion is not working.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.106.0
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Hass.io
- Integration causing this issue: sensor rest
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/rest/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
- platform: rest
  name: Außentemperatur
  json_attributes_path: "$.eta.value"
  json_attributes:
    - '@strValue'
  resource: http://<host>:<port>/<url>
  value_template: '{{ value_json[0].name }}'
  scan_interval: 60

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

Protokolldetails ( WARNING )
Thu Feb 27 2020 22:46:50 GMT+0100 (CET)

REST result could not be parsed as JSON

## Additional information
xmltojson in restful sensor was introduced in #31809 by @bdraco
comments:
https://www.ietf.org/rfc/rfc2376.txt says application/xml is valid as well.

shouldn't be an issue to add

review_comments: Is it meaningful to assert the same value twice? Or rather does it make sense to add `dog` as a json_attrs if it is already defined as the state of the sensor.
@springstan  Its testing both the attribute parsing path and the template lookup even if they point to the same place it still provides coverage of both paths.
Yeah you are correct, I was just wondering why you used the same place for both in comparison to other tests.

Since there wasn't one that did it that way it gave more regression surface in case someone in the future introduces something that interacts poorly between the template and jsonpath.  Seems unlikely but you never know.
